title: Protocol to use de-epithelialized porcine urinary bladder as a tissue scaffold for propagation of pancreatic cells
protocol: Wash porcine urinary bladders collected from a local slaughterhouse.
De-epithelialize urinary bladders by enzymatic treatment.
De-epithelialize urinary bladders mechanically.
Sterilize de-epithelialized urinary bladders for long-term storage in PBS at 4°C.
Use sterilized urinary bladders immediately if not storing.
Ensure use of sterile forceps, scissors, and beakers to prevent microbial contamination.
Collect fresh porcine urinary bladders within 3 hours after isolation.
Transport collected urinary bladders on wet ice.
Avoid freezing urinary bladders before processing.
Process PUBs as soon as possible after isolation to reduce microbial growth.
Transfer PUB inside the laminar flow benches under strict sterile conditions.
Use sterile forceps to transfer PUBs from the transportation bag to a 15-cm cell culture dish filled with DPBS.
Adjust orientation of the PUB so that the urethra faces the operator.
Remove adjacent tissue including fat, urethra, penis, vagina, or ureter.
Transfer the PUB into a new 15-cm dish, filled with DPBS.
Open the bladder neck along the middle line using forceps and scissors.
Unfold the bladder and discard any remaining urine by washing the PUB in DPBS.
Perform a detailed visual inspection to check for bleedings, signs of infection, tumors, or other abnormalities.
Trim small bleedings from the bladder.
Discard the bladder if any other abnormalities are present.
Discard the pub if signs of pus or infection are evident within it.
Clean the laminar flow bench rigorously after discarding a contaminated PUB and removing any tools in contact with the PUB.
Inspect the outer wall of the PUB for signs similar to those on the inner side.
Remove the ureteral ostium from the PUB.
Transfer the PUB into a beaker containing an excess volume of bladder wash solution.
Incubate the PUB at room temperature for at least 5 minutes.
Transfer the PUB to a new beaker with fresh bladder wash solution.
Repeat the washing step three times in total.
Ensure that the PUB is completely submerged in the wash solution during each step.
Transfer PUBs to a beaker filled with the dispase-II working solution.
Incubate the PUBs overnight at 4°C.
Transfer one PUB at a time to a new 15-cm cell culture dish filled with DPBS.
Lift the PUB with forceps above the cell culture dish.
Strip off the epithelial cell layer using a second pair of forceps.
Repeat this step from different angles until complete removal of the epithelial layer.
Transfer de-epithelialized PUBs to a beaker filled with DPBS.
Sway PUBs to remove any remaining urothelial cells.
Repeat the stripping and washing steps in a new beaker with fresh DPBS.
Transfer one PUB at a time into a new 15-cm cell culture dish filled with PBS.
Cut the PUB into pieces of approximately 2 cm² with sterile scissors.
Add 6 mL of HBSS to each well of a 6-well plate.
Precoat wells of a 6-well plate with 3 mL of a 2% Agarose/PBS solution.
Solidify the Agarose in each well.
Fill medium up to 6 mL per well after solidification of the Agarose.
Place one 40-μm cell strainer into one well of the 6-well plate.
Ensure that the lower part of the cell strainer is in contact with the medium, avoiding air bubbles below it.
Place a piece of PUB into each cell strainer of the 6-well plates, ensuring the former urothelial side faces up and the outer wall faces down.
Incubate the plates in a cell culture incubator for 24 hours at 37°C with a 5% CO2 and 21% O2 atmosphere.
Check for signs of microbial contamination by visual inspection.
Inspect wells microscopically for any signs of contamination.
Prepare new 6-well plates containing 6 mL of respective cell culture medium.
Include 3% antibiotic-antimycotic solution in the medium.
Add 10 μM Y-27632 to the medium if using PSC-derived cultures.
Add 10 μM Y-27632 for cell seeding when enhancing the viability of pluripotent stem cell-derived pancreatic cells.

Transfer non-contaminated PUBs into new 6-well plates using sterile forceps, ensuring no air bubbles are present below the nylon meshes and that PUBs are only in contact with medium on the lower site.
Prepare a beaker with around 350 mL sterilization solution for PUBs.
Incubate PUBs in sterilization solution for 24 h at 4°C–8°C.
Repeat sterilization for another 24 h using new sterilization solution.
Wash PUBs twice with DPBS for at least 5 min.
Transfer one PUB at a time to a 15-cm cell culture dish filled with DPBS.
Cut the PUB into pieces of approximately 2 cm² with sterile scissors.
Prepare 6-well plates containing 6 ml of the respective cell culture medium, including 3% antibiotic-antimycotic solution and in case of PSC-derived cultures also 10 μM Y-27632.
Place a cell strainer into each well as indicated in step 4.
Transfer PUB pieces into cell strainers, ensuring that the former urothelial side is facing the air and the tunica serosa is in contact with the medium.
Incubate in a cell culture incubator for 24–72 h at 37°C.
Check for any signs of contamination before proceeding with the cell seeding.
Take quality control samples for histological examination of the de-epithelialization.
Use sterilized tools and work under a sterile laminar flow hood to handle PUBs.
Place two rings on each bladder using sterile forceps.
Note: Rings should be placed straightly on PUBs to prevent cell suspension spilling during seeding.
Digest Matrigel with 1 mg/mL collagenase/dispase for 2-4 hours at 37°C in a cell culture incubator with 5% CO2.
Stop the reaction by adding neutralization solution (twice the amount of collagenase/dispase).
Centrifuge the organoids for 5 minutes at 200 g.
If singularization is necessary, wash the organoids once in DPBS.
Resuspend the organoids in accutase and incubate them for 30 minutes at 37°C in a water bath.
Gently pipette the organoids up and down after 15 minutes of incubation to enhance enzymatic digestion.
Stop the reaction by adding twice the amount of neutralization solution.
Centrifuge the organoids for 5 minutes at 200 g before proceeding.
Count cell/organoid number.
Adjust cell/organoid numbers according to the number of intended rings.
Mix different cell types well by pipetting if co-cultures are intended.
Centrifuge cell suspensions and remove the supernatant completely.
Resuspend cells/organoids in the respective cell culture medium with a volume of 15 μL medium per ring.
Add 10 μM Y-27632 to the medium for PSC-derived cell cultures.
For every ring, add 15 μL GFR-Matrigel to the cell suspension to reach a final concentration of 50% GFR-Matrigel.
Add 30 μL of cell suspension to each ring.
Carefully check for any potential spilling outside the rings and mark respective rings on the cell culture plates.
Place the cell culture plates in a cell culture incubator at 37°C until the next medium change.
Once to twice a week, prepare new 6-well plates containing 6 mL of the respective culture medium for the cell types seeded on the PUBs.
Transfer PUBs from the old plate to the new plate using sterile forceps.
Treat PUBs with drugs or small molecules to investigate cytotoxicity and transgene expression.
Add doxycycline at a concentration of 3 μg/mL to the culture medium to modulate transgene expression.
Test the effects of olaparib at a concentration of 3.7 μM on cancer cells or patient-derived organoids.
Test the effects of irinotecan at a concentration of 1.1 μM on cancer cells or patient-derived organoids.
Add the respective drug or small molecule in the concentration of interest to the medium.
Perform medium change as described in Part II-3a-b.
Alternatively, add the drugs in the desired concentration in a small volume, e.g., 30 μL, to the rings.
Fill the wells of a new 6-well plate with 3.7% formaldehyde.
Take PUB pieces out of the cell strainers and transfer each to one well filled with formaldehyde.
Drown the PUBs very carefully in the formaldehyde solution ensuring complete coverage.
Fix the cells overnight at 4°C–8°C.
Remove the rings from the PUBs after overnight fixation to avoid detachment of adherent cells.
Remove any tissue distant to the rings from the PUBs with scissors or a scalpel.
Cut the piece of PUB in the middle of the former ring area if vertical sectioning and investigation of invasion into the former sub-epithelial stroma or muscle layer is desired.
Perform a standard automated dehydration series.
Place the bladder upper side down (180° inversion) for paraffin embedding.
Turn two halves obtained from cutting the middle of the implantation site by 90° so that the sectioned side faces the bottom during paraffin embedding.
Perform standard histological staining procedures.
Confirm identity of your cells by specific staining using human-specific antibodies such as anti-human nucleoli, anti-human cytokeratin 19, and human-specific Ki-67.
Fill the wells of a 6-well plate with DPBS.
Transfer PUB pieces from cell strainers to the 6-well plate.
Carefully submerge the PUBs in the DPBS and shake the plate to enable proper washing.
Remove the rings from the PUBs very carefully.
Prepare a new 12-well plate.
Fill the wells with 2 mL of collagenase-II working solution.
Take PUBs from the DPBS and place them cell-containing side up into the collagenase-II working solution.
Ensure complete coverage of the PUBs with the collagenase-II solution.
Incubate for 60 min at 37°C on an orbital shaker with 115 rotations per minute.
Shake the plates carefully to allow cells to spread throughout the whole well.
Check under the microscope if cells are floating around.
In case of very few detached cells, prolong the incubation in the collagenase-II solution to up to 180 min.
Use forceps to lift the PUBs and hold it against the edges of the well.
Aspirate the collagenase-II solution containing the cells with a pipette and rinse it against the former ring area of the PUBs to loosen any remaining cells.
Transfer the collagenase-II solution to a 15-mL centrifugation tube.
Use 4 mL neutralization solution to wash the wells and after rinsing the bladders again, transfer the cell suspension to the same tube.
Perform a centrifugation at 200–250 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend in 2 mL DPBS.
Repeat the centrifugation at 200–250 × g.
Aspirate the DPBS.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL accutase.
Incubate the suspension at 37°C in a waterbath for 30 min.
Mix well by pipetting up and down after 15 min.
Take cells from the waterbath and mix again until cells are homogeneously resuspended using a 1,000 μL pipette.
Add 2 mL of neutralization solution and mix well.
Perform centrifugation at 200–250 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in 2 mL DPBS.
Perform standard flow cytometry staining and measurement on cells from the PUBs.
Test antibody specificity for human/murine cells before flow cytometry analysis.
Aspirate supernatant.
Transfer PUBs from cell strainers to 12-well plates filled with DPBS.
Remove tissue not adjacent to the rings with scissors.
Shake PUBs in DPBS and carefully remove the rings.
Transfer PUBs into new wells filled with collagenase-II working solution.
Incubate on a shaker for 1–3 hours.
Collect supernatant containing cells of interest in a centrifugation tube.
Rinse PUBs with neutralization solution.
Add neutralization solution to the centrifugation tube.
Centrifuge and wash cells in DPBS.
Incubate cells in accutase for 30 minutes to achieve singularization.
